title: SLO evaluator: add debounce/holdoff + minimum sample gating to prevent rollout flapping
author: Jordan Lee
description: Context: As part of auto-rollback/pause on SLO breach, the rollout controller’s SLO evaluator was too eager to act on sparse traffic and short transient spikes, causing "pause" decisions to flap during low-volume canaries and early rollout steps. This PR implements the guardrails from ADR-0127 (burn-rate evaluation strategy) specifically around debounce/holdoff and minimum request-volume requirements. Summary of changes: 1) Minimum sample gating: require a minimum number of requests in each evaluation window before a breach can be considered actionable. If sample count is below threshold, the evaluation result is "INSUFFICIENT_DATA" and the controller will not trigger pause/rollback. 2) Debounce/holdoff: introduce configurable holdoff duration after an action (pause/rollback) and a debounce rule requiring consecutive breaches across fast and slow windows before escalating. This reduces oscillation when metrics briefly cross thresholds due to autoscaling/batching effects. 3) Clear suppression reasons: evaluator returns a suppression reason code (e.g., MIN_SAMPLES_NOT_MET, HOLD_OFF_ACTIVE, MONITOR_STALE) that is emitted to metrics and audit events (wired in follow-up PRs) and surfaced in logs for on-call triage. 4) Simulation tests: add deterministic simulation tests that model request volume + latency/error spikes to validate that: a) we don’t act when volume is low, b) we do act on sustained regressions, and c) we do not flap between "BREACH" and "OK" due to jitter. Notes/compatibility: This change is internal to the rollout SLO evaluator module. Policy defaults remain unchanged in this PR, but new config fields are read when present (min_samples, holdoff_seconds, consecutive_breach_count). If a rollout policy does not specify the new fields, conservative defaults are applied (documented inline). Follow-ups: metrics labels are added in pr-28471; audit trail schema integration is in pr-28435 and ADR-0128; end-to-end staging coverage in pr-28490. Testing: unit tests for evaluator transitions; simulation suite for flapping scenarios; CI green. Risk: medium. Most logic is guarded behind the rollout auto-actions feature flag and only affects decisioning when enabled.

review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE): "Can we ensure we gate on BOTH fast and slow windows? We’ve seen 5m burn triggers on short spikes during autoscaling."
Jordan Lee (author): "Yes — implemented a consecutive breach requirement across fast+slow (configurable). Added sim case fast spike then recover; it stays suppressed."
Allison Grant: "Please document the suppression reasons and make sure they’re stable strings; dashboards/alerts will depend on them."
Jordan Lee (author): "Done. Added enum + comment that values are part of the observability contract; also added tests that snapshot reason strings."
Jada Williams: "Holdoff should start after *any* action decision, not only rollback. In MVP we pause first, so we should not keep re-pausing."
Jordan Lee (author): "Updated: holdoff is applied after PAUSE and ROLLBACK decisions. Added scenario 'holdoff_prevents_oscillation' to cover this."
Logan Wright: "Nit: min samples should be per-window; don’t let slow window volume accidentally satisfy fast window."
Jordan Lee (author): "Fixed: sample gating is evaluated independently for each window; decision requires both windows to meet min_samples when confirmation is enabled."
Sean Gallagher (SRE): "Looks good. One more ask: default min_samples should be conservative (avoid acting under low traffic), but not so high that Dedicated never triggers at night."
Jordan Lee (author): "Default set to 200 req (fast) / 800 req (slow) for now; can be overridden by tier templates. Added note in README that defaults may be revisited with real traffic."
Allison Grant: "Approved once the README note is in."
Jordan Lee (author): "Added README tuning guidance + link to ADR-0127."
release_notes: Rollout SLO evaluation now includes minimum request-volume gating and debounce/holdoff to prevent auto-actions from flapping during low-volume or transient spikes.
